To: lindqvist-family-blog
Replying to: none
Cc: none
Subject: So... Fernhollow Photo is a real business now!!

OK, family. I have news. Big news. The kind of news I was trying to figure out how to tell you without Dad cornering me next to the turkey at Aunt Ruthie’s, so I’m putting it here first.

I started my own photography business!!! It’s called Fernhollow Photo, the LLC is filed, the website is up, and apparently I am a person who owns a business now. Still getting used to that last part.

Dad, before you say anything: I have health insurance. I picked a marketplace plan and it starts January 1. Please enjoy your stuffing in peace.

Here’s how we got here. Marisol told me on October 6 that she was closing Rosebud Lane at the end of the month. I’d been shooting for her for four years, so that was a pretty huge thing to hear. I love that studio and I’m going to miss it, and I’m especially going to miss getting to work with Marisol all the time.

Marisol basically taught me everything. How to keep my head when a wedding day goes sideways, how to find the good light, how to make people feel comfortable when there’s a camera in their face. Also probably how to carry way too much equipment without falling over, although the jury is still out on that one. She trusted me with so much over those four years and then trusted me with couples she couldn’t keep for 2027. Six of the weddings I have booked came from her referrals. Marisol, if you’re reading this, thank you for everything. I love you.

The other eight weddings found me on their own, which is a sentence I keep looking at because it doesn’t quite feel real yet. Fourteen weddings booked for 2027 already!! June is going to be a lot, apparently. Four weddings in one month. Knees, I hope you’re listening.

My first booking that was completely mine is Dahlia and Ken. They’re getting married June 12 at Timberline, and they found me because of the pictures I took of a couple at Multnomah Falls. Someone saw my photos and thought, yes, that’s who we want there on our wedding day. I may have stared at that email for a while.

And yes, I have help for the big weddings! Jae will be second shooting with me and gets paid per wedding. I’m not planning to clone myself or somehow photograph both ends of the aisle at once. Though if anyone figures out the cloning thing, let me know before June.

I know this probably sounds like a very sudden announcement, especially since Rosebud Lane only just closed. But I’ve been planning this in my head for two years. I didn’t know exactly when it would happen, and I definitely didn’t picture filing my LLC on my lunch break in the car outside a Fred Meyer, but that is where it happened. October 22. Very glamorous. I cried a little and then had to go back to work like a normal person.

Sam made me a cake to celebrate and had them write FERNHOLLOW on it. Except the cake said FERNHOLOW. One L short, still delicious. We ate it anyway, obviously. I’m considering keeping a picture of it forever.

And Grandma, the name is for you. It’s from the fern hollow trail behind your old place in Gresham, where I took my first real pictures with your Pentax. I kept thinking about that trail when I was trying to pick a name, and nothing else felt right. You let me borrow your camera and wander around taking pictures of everything, even when I’m pretty sure half of them were just blurry leaves. So this little business has a piece of you in it.

I’m scared, I won’t pretend I’m not. It’s a big change and there’s a lot to learn about running the business side of things. But I have a plan, I have weddings on the calendar, I have Jae for the big days, and I have health insurance, Dad. I’m not doing this on a whim. Mostly I’m just really, really excited that I get to give this a try.

Also! If anyone wants free family pictures at Thanksgiving, I’ll bring my camera to Ruthie’s. We can do them before dinner while everyone still has clean clothes. Uncle Greg, I’ll try to work quickly if you’re “freezing” again.

Love you all. Can’t wait to see you in a couple of weeks. And yes, Mom, Sam is coming. We’ll bring the rolls and the cranberry thing!
